title: A cooperative's outages, restored in steps

blocks.text: A rural electric cooperative serves `customers_served` customers. When a storm takes a line down its crews rarely restore everyone at once: they switch some customers onto another feeder within minutes, fix the main line an hour later, and reach the last houses after that. So each outage in the cooperative's log is a list of restoration **steps**: `Step(customers, minute)` says that `customers` customers came back on supply `minute` minutes after the outage began. Every customer in an outage lost power at its start.

Write `indices(outages, customers_served)` in `outages.py`, returning the year's SAIFI, SAIDI and CAIDI as `{"SAIFI": ..., "SAIDI": ..., "CAIDI": ...}`. The cooperative follows the IEEE rule for what counts: a customer who is back on supply within five minutes (five included) had a momentary interruption, which counts in none of the three indices, even when other customers of the same outage waited much longer. CAIDI is the average wait of an interrupted customer, and 0 in a year with no sustained interruption.
Work the first test's outage by hand before you code: 600 customers restored at 30 minutes and 400 at 90, out of 10,000 served. How many customer interruptions is that, and how many customer-minutes?

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from outages import Step, indices

storm = [Step(300, 3), Step(900, 45), Step(300, 120)]
fault = [Step(500, 25)]

print("storm only, 20000 served:", indices([storm], 20_000))
print("storm and fault, 20000 served:", indices([storm, fault], 20_000))
print("a 3-minute blip, 20000 served:", indices([[Step(1_000, 3)]], 20_000))

cases.says: an outage restored in two steps counts each group of customers for the minutes it waited
a year of several staged outages gives the indices worked out by hand
customers restored within five minutes of an outage that lasted longer for others are left out
customers restored at exactly five minutes are left out
CAIDI averages the wait over every interrupted customer, not over outages, and is 0 in a year of blinks
